title: Semantic HTML
definition: The use of HTML markup to reinforce the semantics, or meaning, of the information in webpages rather than merely defining its presentation or look.
simpleExplanation: You can build an entire website using only `<div>` tags. Visually, it might look perfect. But a blind person using a screen reader won't know where the navigation bar is, and Google's search engine won't know what part of the page is the main article. Semantic HTML uses specific tags like `<nav>`, `<article>`, and `<footer>` so machines understand your website.
realWorldExample: Replacing a `<div class="navigation">` with a `<nav>` tag. They look exactly the same to a sighted user, but the `<nav>` tag drastically improves SEO and Accessibility.
useCases: Making websites accessible for visually impaired users

intermediate: Why is it bad practice to use a `<div>` for a button?

answers.question: Why not use a div for a button?
answers.answer: A `<div>` is semantically meaningless. If you style a `<div>` to look like a button, users navigating via keyboard (pressing 'Tab') cannot focus on it, and hitting 'Enter' won't click it. A `<button>` tag has all of this built-in natively.
